item.title: Lost Eloise portrait found in dumpster sells for $100,000 after decades in closet
item.description: In a fascinating twist of fate, Eloise's original portrait, crafted by Hilary Knight in 1956, mysteriously disappeared during a Junior League Ball in 1960. Rediscovered in a dumpster, it lay dormant in Knight's closet for years, only to be brought back to life at a 2017 exhibition at the New-York Historical Society. Its subsequent auction at Bonhams in 2018 for $100,000 underscores the unpredictable journey and enduring value of art.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Insurer denies heart procedure for 12-year-old with Kawasaki disease
item.description: Rowan Lowry, a 12-year-old boy, urgently needs a stent procedure to address complications stemming from Kawasaki disease. His family faces an insurance denial categorizing the procedure as medically unnecessary. Undeterred, they plan to seek treatment at Boston Children's Hospital, driven by their concern for Rowan's deteriorating health and the fear of open-heart surgery. Determined, they vow to advocate fiercely for their son's well-being despite the financial strain.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Teen Builds Rural Stem Access: Ontario student launches Project RISE; initiative widens STEM opportunities
item.description: At just 17 years old, Amara Wilson-Zegil is on a mission to bridge the gap in STEM education for children in rural areas. With an impressive outreach to over 1,800 students through robotics initiatives and camps, she has launched Project RISE. This groundbreaking initiative aims to combat educational disparities by providing vital tech experiences, ensuring more youth in Northern Ontario can access quality STEM opportunities.

item.title: Pakistan plans Moon landing by 2035, expands space cooperation with China
item.description: Pakistan aims to land on the Moon by 2035 and send its first astronaut for a space mission. The astronaut, selected from candidates trained in China, is expected to participate in scientific experiments. Cooperation with China enhances Pakistan's aspirations in space exploration and technological advancement. Additionally, plans for establishing the first Space Museum at the University of Narowal were announced to promote scientific awareness.
item.dc:creator: Yashasvi Vasistha

item.title: Brazilian man sells all, travels 1,200 miles to marry online girlfriend, discovers she was AI-generated
item.description: A Brazilian man sold all his belongings and travelled over 1,200 miles to meet the online girlfriend he hoped to marry. Edimar Martins, 49, discovered that the woman, featured on a TikTok account with around 300,000 followers, was AI-generated. After running out of money, he received assistance to return home but remains hopeful about finding love.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Florida opens $191.8M water plant to protect the Matanzas River and conserve drinking water
item.description: St. Johns County Utilities officials celebrated the completion of the State Road 207 Water Reclamation Facility. This facility, costing $191.8 million, will treat wastewater and provide reclaimed water for irrigation purposes. The project aims to reduce dependence on the Floridan Aquifer, especially during ongoing drought conditions. Capacity of the facility can be expanded to meet future demand while preventing nutrient pollution in local waters.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Florida appeals court overturns $2,675 monthly alimony after a 249-day marriage
item.description: A recent decision by a Florida appeals court reversed an alimony order for a short marriage lasting 249 days. The court found insufficient evidence regarding the former wife's need for financial support. The trial court had awarded nine months of temporary alimony based on prior cases instead of specific proof. The appeals court emphasized the importance of individual cases and relevant evidence in such rulings.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Egypt pledges support for Saudi Arabia as Houthi attacks escalate
item.description: Egypt announced its willingness to provide military assistance to Saudi Arabia to ensure its security and stability. President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi convened the National Defence Council to discuss potential support amid Houthi assaults. These attacks have targeted key infrastructure, including Riyadh’s international airport and Saudi Aramco. Egypt has previously supported Saudi Arabia in the Yemeni conflict, although its role has been limited.
item.dc:creator: Pranjal Pandey

item.title: Michigan court allows Kalamazoo County to seize a family’s lakefront cottage for park expansion
item.description: The Michigan Court of Appeals has confirmed Kalamazoo County's legal right to acquire a residential cottage located near Prairie View County Park, ending a protracted legal battle. County officials want to integrate the cottage into their plans for park expansion, but the owners have raised objections, arguing that the public purpose claims are obsolete. The issue of fair compensation continues to be debated if a mutual valuation is not achieved.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Meet Sgiath: The mountain rescue Labrador who has won IFAW’s 2026 Animal of the Year Award
item.description: Sgiath, a remarkable six-year-old black Labrador, has recently made headlines for her extraordinary ability to detect invasive sea squirt, leading her to win the prestigious 2026 Animal of the Year Award. Partnering with marine ecologist Dr. Texa Sim, Sgiath's keen sense of smell plays a vital role in identifying this invasive organism. Her early detection skills contribute significantly to marine conservation efforts.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: In 2001, Tony Bennett and his wife opened an arts school for 250 students; how it looks 25 years later
item.description: Tony Bennett and Susan Benedetto co-founded the Frank Sinatra School of the Arts in 2001 in New York. The school offers specialized training in various art forms while maintaining a strong academic curriculum. Students can major in dance, drama, film, fine art, vocal music, or instrumental music. The school moved to a permanent facility in 2009, equipped with state-of-the-art spaces for performance and production.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Texas Supreme Court to decide if city can seize land for a privately run golf facility
item.description: The Texas Supreme Court will examine an eminent domain case involving Westworth Village's attempt to acquire land from Jim Burgess for a golf facility. Following a previous ruling that deemed the taking unconstitutional on public use grounds, the case delves into the legality of local governments appropriating private property for private enterprise projects. This decision holds the potential to set a major precedent for eminent domain laws throughout Texas.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: JD Vance’s immigration tiger is turning on its rider
item.description: US Vice President JD Vance admitted his rhetoric on H-1B visas was flawed during a recent town hall event. An Indian-American woman challenged him on his stance, suggesting it scapegoats immigrants. Vance defended his position by claiming he was criticizing corporate practices rather than foreign workers. His remarks have led to significant backlash from various groups regarding his mixed heritage.
item.dc:creator: Chidanand Rajghatta

item.title: Russia sold Alaska for peanuts. Now it guards America against Moscow
item.description: In 1867, Russia sold Alaska to the United States for $7.2 million, reflecting strategic concerns. The decision stemmed from fears of potential conflict with Britain during the Crimean War. Subsequent discoveries of natural resources transformed Alaska's economic importance significantly over the years. Alaska emerged as a crucial military platform for the United States against the Russian Far East.
item.dc:creator: Pranjal Pandey

item.title: In 2015, Taylor Swift gave $50,000 to Seattle Symphony; 11 years later, its school programme lives on
item.description: In December 2015, Taylor Swift made a notable donation of $50,000 to the Seattle Symphony. This contribution supported the Link Up education programme, which introduces orchestral music to young students. The funding also benefitted the musicians' pension fund as part of the symphony's broader mission. Over the years, Link Up has successfully engaged thousands of children through interactive music experiences.

item.title: Charity shop raises £85,860 from donated banknotes, including one featuring young Queen Elizabeth II
item.description: An anonymous donation of nearly 160 lots of rare banknotes to a British Heart Foundation charity shop in Edinburgh has raised £85,860 at auction. The collection included a banknote featuring a young Queen Elizabeth II and rare currency specimens from Iraq and Saudi Arabia. Staff initially had no idea of its value. The proceeds will support research into heart and circulatory diseases.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Iran offers to reopen Strait of Hormuz in seven days if US accepts conditions
item.description: Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araqchi reiterated that the proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz remains in place. Tehran is analyzing the US response regarding its conditions for ending the conflict. These conditions include lifting sanctions and ending aggression in the region. Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump expressed optimism about a swift resolution to the war and lower gas prices.
